function.name: calculate_slope_gradient
function.description: Calculate the slope gradient between two geographical coordinates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

point1.description: The geographic coordinates for the first point [Latitude, Longitude].

point2.description: The geographic coordinates for the second point [Latitude, Longitude].

unit.description: The unit for the slope gradient. Default is 'degree'.

message.content:
I’m happy to calculate the slope gradient for you, but I’ll need the elevation (height above sea level) for each of the two points.  
The slope gradient is defined as the vertical change divided by the horizontal distance, so without the elevation values I can’t compute it.  

Could you provide the elevations for:

1. (40.7128 N, –74.0060 W) – [City of New York]  
2. (34.0522 N, –118.2437 W) – [City of Los Angeles]  

Once I have those, I’ll calculate the slope gradient in degrees for you.
